versions.changelog: TLS 1.3 PSK session tickets: tls13_psk_from_ticket, tls13_early_secret_from_psk, tls13_binder_key, tls13_psk_binder; NewSessionTicket parser; p256_ecdsa_sign with low-s normalization
TLS 1.2 mTLS / ECDSA client auth: NewSessionTicket capture in session_tickets(), connect_with_client_cert(), CertificateRequest12 parser, CertificateVerify builder, _ecdsa_raw_to_der
ALPN extension support: alpn_protocols param in connect()/connect_with_client_cert(), negotiated_protocol() method; TLS 1.3 + 1.2 ALPN ClientHello builder and ServerHello parser (RFC 7301)
macOS compatibility: load_system_ca_bundle uses /etc/ssl/cert.pem on macOS; fix open() flags in test helpers for macOS ARM64
Fix comptime if scope bug in load_system_ca_bundle (v1.3.1 regression)
Fix load_system_ca_bundle passing a non-NUL-terminated path to open() (failed on Linux)
Accept certificate chains anchored at a cross-signed root (fixes HTTPS on Linux for e.g. Google Trust Services chains); exact byte comparison for keys

SECURITY (critical): certificate path validation now enforces CA constraints (basicConstraints, keyUsage, EKU, pathLen, name chaining, critical extensions); earlier versions let any trusted leaf certificate impersonate any host. Validity times fail closed.

SECURITY: recv_all() requires an authenticated close_notify (truncation; allow_truncation=True opts out); plaintext/undecryptable post-handshake alerts rejected; RSA PKCS#1 out-of-bounds read fixed; all-zero X25519 secret rejected; TLS 1.3 downgrade sentinel checked; TLS 1.3 padding stripped; no PKCS#1 in TLS 1.3 CertificateVerify; *.com wildcards rejected. Interop: RSA-PSS in TLS 1.2 ServerKeyExchange.

TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate (server key rotation no longer breaks connections; update requests answered). Socket I/O: resumable read timeouts reported as 'tls: read timed out', no SIGPIPE on writes to closed peers, EINTR retried, TlsSocket.set_timeout().

SECURITY: constant-time AES (bitsliced), GHASH (table-free) and P-256 secret-key operations (key generation, ECDH, ECDSA signing); removes cache-timing and scalar-length timing leaks. AES-GCM ~8x and P-256 ~3x faster.

TLS 1.3 HelloRetryRequest (P-256/P-384); TLS 1.2 extended master secret and renegotiation_info; constant-time P-384 key exchange. Fixes: TLS 1.2 SHA-384 suites used the SHA-256 PRF; servers with P-384 ECDSA certificates could not connect.

SECURITY: fixes from a second review. A malformed certificate crashed the process; unbounded handshake buffering before authentication; strict TLS 1.2/1.3 state machines (also fixes servers that fragment handshake messages, e.g. facebook.com); nameConstraints and intermediate EKU enforced; RSA >= 2048; strict protocol/DER/signature parsing; TLS 1.2 mTLS over SHA-384 suites fixed.

SHA-512 signatures (RSA PKCS#1/PSS, ecdsa-with-SHA512 and RSA-PSS SHA-512 certificates, TLS 1.3/1.2 rsa_pss_rsae_sha512 and TLS 1.2 rsa_pkcs1_sha512); AES-GCM keys prepared once per connection (64-byte records 4.9 -> 2.9 us); every peer-facing parser fuzzed in CI.

Works alongside Mojo's std: declares no C function std declares (open/read/write, errno), so programs using tls with open(), listdir or get_errno compile again. Sockets use recv/send everywhere; CA bundles over 2 MB are no longer cut off. websocket <= 1.1.3 clashes with it: use websocket >= 1.2.0.

Hardware AES-GCM (ARMv8 crypto / x86 AES-NI + PCLMULQDQ, constant time; software path kept for other targets) and a rewritten receive path: recv loop 34 -> ~1,000 MB/s, recv_all 1 -> 719 MB/s, small reads 22 -> 0.2 us; recv_exact no longer reserves peer-supplied lengths up front. No API change.
